extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists, researchers, and anyone seeking reliable fact-checking or information about Snopes' practices
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the standards and public-facing practices Snopes uses when producing fact checks and investigative reporting, including sourcing, transparency, ratings, and disclosures. Aimed at explaining how Snopes ensures evidence-based, contextualized analysis and how readers can engage or complain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link to and document sources
rubrics_metrics.description: We always link to and document our sources so readers are empowered to do independent research and make up their own minds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite and link to primary and secondary sources for claims; provide documentation that allows readers to verify the underlying evidence themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-based and contextualized analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: When misinformation obscures the truth and readers don’t know what to trust, Snopes’ fact-checking and original investigative reporting lights the way to evidence-based and contextualized analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis should be grounded in evidence and place claims in appropriate context rather than merely asserting truth/falsehood without background or explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about process and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Snopes emphasizes transparency (Our Process, Transparency, Frequently Asked Qs) as part of its public-facing materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain methods, link to process documentation and FAQs so readers understand how investigations and ratings are reached; maintain visible pages for process, disclosures, and team information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact Check Ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Snopes uses a Fact Check Ratings system (menu item: Fact Check Ratings) to evaluate claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply a consistent rating framework to fact checks; make ratings visible and explain what each rating means (page references rating as a core element but does not enumerate rating categories here).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with IFCN standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Snopes is a member of IFCN and in compliance with the International Fact Checking Network's highest standards of combating misinformation online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to IFCN principles (e.g., nonpartisanship, transparency of sources and funding, corrections policy). If readers wish to file an IFCN complaint, they may, but Snopes requests direct contact first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership and disclosure of affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: Snopes.com is an independent publication owned and operated under 'Snopes, Inc' which is a wholly-owned subsidiary of 'Snopes Media Group, Inc' (SMG). SMG is owned by Chris Richmond (60%) and Drew Schoentrup (40%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicly disclose ownership, funding, and relevant affiliations to help readers assess potential conflicts of interest; maintain a Disclosures page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness to public input and corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: The site provides ways for the public to engage (Send Us a Tip) and encourages contact for questions or concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear channels for tips, questions, and complaints; respond to reader inquiries and document corrections as part of transparency practices.
